title: Meridian Health System: Enterprise Transformation Readiness Overview
executive_summary: Meridian operates as an integrated delivery network and health plan with seven active transformation hypotheses awaiting evidence certification.
what_context_reveals: Planning-grade signals span clinical, claims, finance, and analytics modernization; no dimension is yet decision-grade.
why_it_matters: Without certified foundations, AI-led transformation sequencing remains a hypothesis, not an executable roadmap.
decision_implication: Leadership cannot commit capital or sequencing until governance, platform, and data evidence are validated.
evidence_still_needed: Medallion architecture, identity spine, semantic layer, governance model, and baseline metrics all need validation.
module_usage: Nexus Knowledge module should anchor enterprise context before any advisory or sourcing action proceeds.
next_validation_action: Convene cross-functional evidence sprint covering data, platform, governance, and finance owners simultaneously.

title: Who Meridian Is as an Enterprise
executive_summary: Meridian is a medium-to-large integrated delivery network operating clinical delivery and health-plan functions under one enterprise.
what_context_reveals: Dual operating model creates complexity across clinical, member, finance, and analytics domains simultaneously.
why_it_matters: IDN-plus-health-plan complexity amplifies data fragmentation risk across every transformation initiative.
decision_implication: Enterprise profile demands a unified governance model before any cross-domain AI use case can be trusted.
evidence_still_needed: Organizational boundary map between clinical delivery and health-plan operations needs validation.
module_usage: Knowledge module should maintain enterprise profile as the anchor for all dimension context.
next_validation_action: Request org-boundary and operating-model documentation from strategy and operations leadership.

title: Core Business Functions Driving Transformation Demand
executive_summary: Clinical delivery, health-plan operations, finance, and analytics modernization are the four active transformation-demand functions.
what_context_reveals: Each function surfaces distinct data and governance gaps that block cross-functional decision-grade intelligence.
why_it_matters: Function-level fragmentation means no single initiative can succeed without cross-function evidence alignment.
decision_implication: Prioritization must sequence function readiness before committing to enterprise-wide AI deployment.
evidence_still_needed: Function-level process maps, ownership registers, and baseline performance metrics are not yet evidenced.
module_usage: Knowledge module should map function boundaries to use-case dependencies before advisory proceeds.
next_validation_action: Conduct function-owner interviews to capture process maps and baseline performance signals.

title: Ownership Accountability Across Transformation Initiatives
executive_summary: Ownership accountability for data domains, platforms, and governance is not yet evidenced across Meridian's seven initiatives.
what_context_reveals: Attribution, semantic layer, and cost-allocation ownership gaps suggest diffuse accountability across functions.
why_it_matters: Without named owners, governance decisions stall and AI audit requirements cannot be satisfied.
decision_implication: Ownership mapping is a prerequisite before any use case can advance from hypothesis to governed deployment.
evidence_still_needed: RACI or ownership register for data domains, platforms, and governance bodies needs validation.
module_usage: Knowledge module should surface ownership gaps as blockers in every use-case readiness assessment.
next_validation_action: Request RACI documentation from CIO, CDO, and CFO offices covering all seven initiative domains.

title: Workforce Capability Gaps Affecting AI Readiness
executive_summary: Analytics, data engineering, and governance roles supporting transformation are not yet evidenced as adequately staffed.
what_context_reveals: Outsourced analytics managed services dependency suggests internal capability gaps in data and AI functions.
why_it_matters: Workforce gaps in governance and engineering roles create sequencing risk for every modernization initiative.
decision_implication: Capability assessment must precede AI deployment commitments to avoid execution failure.
evidence_still_needed: Role inventory, skill gap assessment, and managed services scope boundaries need validation.
module_usage: Knowledge module should flag workforce readiness as a dependency in program and AI use-case blocks.
next_validation_action: Request workforce capability inventory and managed services scope from CHRO and CIO offices.

title: Application Landscape Complexity and Integration Risk
executive_summary: Fourteen identified systems span Epic, SQL Server, Tableau, SAS, Power BI, claims, pharmacy, CRM, and AWS without proven integration.
what_context_reveals: Multi-vendor, multi-platform landscape creates integration dependencies that are planning-grade, not certified.
why_it_matters: Unproven integrations between Epic, claims, and analytics platforms block every lakehouse and AI use case.
decision_implication: Integration architecture must be validated before any cross-system data product can be trusted.
evidence_still_needed: Integration topology, API inventory, and data-flow diagrams across all fourteen systems need validation.
module_usage: Knowledge module should maintain application dependency map as a live readiness signal.
next_validation_action: Request integration architecture documentation and API inventory from CIO and enterprise architecture teams.

title: Data Asset Fragmentation Blocking Decision-Grade Intelligence
executive_summary: Clinical, claims, pharmacy, member identity, and financial data assets are fragmented with no certified harmonization layer.
what_context_reveals: Patient and member identity spine is not yet evidenced, making longitudinal views a hypothesis only.
why_it_matters: Without a governed identity spine, every AI use case risks operating on misaligned or duplicate records.
decision_implication: Identity resolution and data harmonization must be certified before any AI model is trained or deployed.
evidence_still_needed: Identity spine design, claims-pharmacy harmonization rules, and data quality certifications need validation.
module_usage: Knowledge module should surface data asset gaps as the primary blocker in lakehouse and AI readiness blocks.
next_validation_action: Commission data asset inventory and identity resolution design review with CDO and data engineering leads.

title: Platform Foundation Readiness Is Not Yet Evidenced
executive_summary: AWS analytics foundation and Databricks aspiration are planning-grade; no certified medallion architecture exists.
what_context_reveals: On-prem SQL Server marts coexist with cloud aspirations, creating hybrid complexity without proven migration path.
why_it_matters: An uncertified platform foundation means AI and lakehouse use cases have no reliable execution environment.
decision_implication: Platform readiness certification must precede any production AI deployment commitment.
evidence_still_needed: AWS environment design, Databricks configuration, network controls, and security posture need validation.
module_usage: Knowledge module should flag platform readiness as a hard dependency gate for all AI use cases.
next_validation_action: Request AWS and Databricks environment assessment from CIO and cloud engineering teams.

title: Vendor Dependency Map Requires Evidence Before Advisory Action
executive_summary: Seven vendors including Epic, Microsoft, SAS, AWS, and Databricks are identified; contract terms are not yet evidenced.
what_context_reveals: Outsourced analytics managed services dependency adds a vendor layer whose scope boundaries are not certified.
why_it_matters: Unvalidated contract terms create sequencing risk when renegotiating or consolidating vendor relationships.
decision_implication: Vendor dependency and contract evidence must be gathered before sourcing or consolidation decisions are made.
evidence_still_needed: Contract terms, renewal dates, SLA commitments, and managed services scope need validation.
module_usage: Knowledge module should maintain vendor dependency map as input to any future sourcing advisory.
next_validation_action: Request vendor contract register and managed services scope documentation from procurement and CIO offices.

title: IT Spend Baseline and Value Proof Are Not Yet Evidenced
executive_summary: No audited IT spend baseline, budget allocation, or value realization evidence is available for Meridian's transformation portfolio.
what_context_reveals: Without spend baseline, ROI hypotheses for all seven use cases remain unquantifiable at this stage.
why_it_matters: CFO-level investment decisions require spend baseline and value proof before capital can be committed.
decision_implication: Finance and IT must jointly establish spend baseline before any use-case ROI claim can be made.
evidence_still_needed: IT budget allocation, vendor spend by domain, and value realization tracking need validation.
module_usage: Knowledge module should surface spend baseline gap as a CFO-facing blocker in every finance use-case block.
next_validation_action: Request IT budget and vendor spend data from CFO and IT finance teams for baseline establishment.

title: Seven Transformation Initiatives Are Planning-Grade, Not Execution-Ready
executive_summary: All seven Meridian initiatives from lakehouse to automated close are hypothesis-stage pending evidence certification.
what_context_reveals: No initiative has certified platform, governance, or data foundation evidence required for execution commitment.
why_it_matters: Committing resources to unvalidated initiatives risks capital misallocation and transformation sequencing failure.
decision_implication: Program governance must gate each initiative on evidence certification before execution funding is approved.
evidence_still_needed: Initiative charters, milestone plans, owner assignments, and readiness gates need validation.
module_usage: Knowledge module should maintain program readiness matrix as the primary portfolio governance signal.
next_validation_action: Establish program governance board with evidence-gate criteria for all seven initiatives.

title: AI Use Cases Require Governance and Data Foundation Before Deployment
executive_summary: Prior-auth, coding, UM automation, and call center AI are hypotheses blocked by absent governance and semantic layer.
what_context_reveals: No AI audit trail, certified semantic layer, or data quality rules exist to support responsible AI deployment.
why_it_matters: Deploying AI without audit trail and governance exposes Meridian to regulatory and clinical risk.
decision_implication: AI deployment must be gated on governance certification, audit trail design, and semantic layer validation.
evidence_still_needed: AI governance framework, audit trail design, semantic layer certification, and quality rules need validation.
module_usage: Knowledge module should surface AI readiness gaps as hard blockers in every automation use-case assessment.
next_validation_action: Commission AI governance and audit trail design review with CDO, compliance, and clinical informatics leads.

title: Control Gaps Span Data, Platform, Governance, and AI Domains
executive_summary: No certified security, network, data governance, or AI control evidence is available across Meridian's transformation scope.
what_context_reveals: PHI-adjacent transformation without certified controls creates regulatory exposure across all seven initiatives.
why_it_matters: Healthcare regulatory requirements demand certified controls before any AI or data product touches member or patient data.
decision_implication: Risk and compliance leadership must certify control posture before any initiative advances to production.
evidence_still_needed: Security posture, data governance controls, AI audit requirements, and PHI handling protocols need validation.
module_usage: Knowledge module should surface control gaps as compliance-blocking signals in every use-case readiness block.
next_validation_action: Request control inventory and compliance posture assessment from CISO, compliance, and legal teams.

title: Stakeholder and Partner Relationships Require Evidence Mapping
executive_summary: Provider network, health-plan member, and vendor relationships are identified but not yet evidenced in governed form.
what_context_reveals: Provider contract linkage and member identity relationships are fragmented across multiple unintegrated systems.
why_it_matters: Ungoverned relationship data blocks provider performance, cost transparency, and member experience use cases.
decision_implication: Relationship data governance must be established before provider or member-facing AI use cases can proceed.
evidence_still_needed: Provider contract linkage, member identity resolution, and partner data-sharing agreements need validation.
module_usage: Knowledge module should map relationship dependencies to use-case readiness gates.
next_validation_action: Request provider contract and member identity governance documentation from network and health-plan operations.

title: Evidence Sources Are Planning-Grade Across All Dimensions
executive_summary: All current Meridian context is planning-grade; no certified production evidence source has been validated.
what_context_reveals: Interview signals and use-case hypotheses are the primary evidence inputs; no audited data sources are confirmed.
why_it_matters: Advisory and investment decisions made on planning-grade evidence carry high sequencing and capital risk.
decision_implication: Evidence certification sprint must precede any executive commitment or transformation investment decision.
evidence_still_needed: Certified data sources, system inventories, governance documentation, and baseline metrics need validation.
module_usage: Knowledge module should maintain evidence source registry and confidence ratings for all dimensions.
next_validation_action: Launch structured evidence collection sprint with owners across all fourteen identified systems.

title: Baseline Metrics Are Absent Across Clinical, Finance, and Operations
executive_summary: No certified baseline metrics exist for AHT, first-call resolution, HEDIS, STAR, margin, or close-cycle performance.
what_context_reveals: Without baselines, value hypotheses for all seven initiatives cannot be quantified or validated post-deployment.
why_it_matters: Metric absence blocks CFO-level ROI validation and clinical quality improvement measurement.
decision_implication: Baseline metric capture must be a first-order deliverable before any initiative value case is presented.
evidence_still_needed: Operational, clinical, and financial baseline metrics across all seven initiative domains need validation.
module_usage: Knowledge module should surface metric baseline gaps as value-proof blockers in every use-case block.
next_validation_action: Commission baseline metric capture across clinical, operations, and finance with domain owners.

executive_summary: Integrated delivery networks face known fragmentation, regulatory, and data governance challenges that align with Meridian's gap profile.
what_context_reveals: Industry patterns suggest medallion architecture, identity spine, and semantic layer are common IDN transformation prerequisites.
why_it_matters: Meridian's gap profile mirrors known IDN failure patterns when governance and platform foundations are skipped.
decision_implication: Industry pattern evidence supports prioritizing foundation work over AI deployment to avoid known failure modes.
evidence_still_needed: Meridian-specific regulatory posture and competitive benchmarking data need validation against industry patterns.
module_usage: Knowledge module should apply IDN industry patterns as advisory context in every dimension readiness block.
next_validation_action: Benchmark Meridian's gap profile against IDN peer transformation evidence with strategy and analytics leadership.

executive_summary: Clinical informatics, actuarial, data engineering, and AI governance expert lenses are needed to validate transformation hypotheses.
what_context_reveals: No single executive lens covers the full scope of Meridian's cross-domain transformation complexity.
why_it_matters: Without expert validation, planning-grade hypotheses risk advancing to execution without sufficient scrutiny.
decision_implication: Multi-lens expert review must be structured before any initiative moves from hypothesis to funded program.
evidence_still_needed: Expert engagement plan covering clinical, actuarial, technology, and governance domains needs validation.
module_usage: Knowledge module should surface expert lens requirements as advisory inputs to each use-case readiness block.
next_validation_action: Identify and engage clinical informatics, actuarial, and AI governance experts for hypothesis validation sessions.

executive_summary: An outsourced analytics managed services provider is identified but scope, SLAs, and boundaries are not yet evidenced.
what_context_reveals: Managed services dependency may create capability gaps or transition risk as Meridian modernizes its analytics estate.
why_it_matters: Undefined managed services scope creates risk when insourcing, renegotiating, or replacing analytics capabilities.
decision_implication: Managed services scope must be documented before analytics modernization sequencing decisions are made.
evidence_still_needed: Managed services contract scope, SLA terms, capability inventory, and transition risk assessment need validation.
module_usage: Knowledge module should surface managed services scope as a dependency in analytics and AI readiness blocks.
next_validation_action: Request managed services contract and scope documentation from procurement and analytics leadership.

executive_summary: Prior-auth, close cycle, call center, and payment integrity workflows lack certified process evidence for AI readiness assessment.
what_context_reveals: Manual reporting maintenance and fragmented BI tools signal process inefficiency but without quantified baseline evidence.
why_it_matters: AI automation cannot be responsibly scoped without certified process maps, cycle times, and exception rates.
decision_implication: Process evidence capture must precede AI workflow automation design for all seven initiative domains.
evidence_still_needed: Process maps, cycle time baselines, exception rates, and workflow ownership for all key processes need validation.
module_usage: Knowledge module should surface process evidence gaps as automation-readiness blockers in every operational use case.
